parser already does for a negative length ("proto: negative length found
during unmarshaling"). Adding the same guards to both helpers in the fix
verification copy makes both unit reproductions pass with that error. Severity:
availability only (no log or state corruption), but any peer that can reach
the Raft port can kill the process in the default (non-TLS) configuration.

This turn re-validated the oldest network-crash finding end to end, in both directions, in a single session.

**F6 re-verified live**

- Captured tree: the 15-byte frame produces `panic: runtime error: index out of range [-9223372036854775797]` in `MessageBatch.messageCount` → `Unmarshal` → `serveConn` (log: [e2e_vuln_stderr.txt](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/audit/cover/f06/e2e_vuln_stderr.txt)).
- Fixed copy: the identical frame yields `NODEHOST SURVIVED THE MALFORMED BATCH` (log: [e2e_fixed_stdout.txt](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/audit/cover/f06/e2e_fixed_stdout.txt)).

The F6 section in the report now carries this re-verification, and `audit/tools/e2ecrash` was copied into `audit/diag-fixes/` so both halves reproduce from the same harness.

**Static spot-check (negative)**

I also scanned the rest of `raftpb/raft_optimized.go` for other hand-written decode paths with unchecked slices. The generated-style sites (`Entries`, `Snapshot`, `Requests`, `SourceAddress`) all sit behind `postIndex` bounds checks; the custom `messageCount`/`entryCount` helpers remain the only ones missing them, i.e. exactly what F6 reports — no sibling defect to add.

Combined with the earlier certification (all 43 audit tests green on the fixed copy, 15/15 repros fixed) and the regenerated per-package matrix, the audit now has: 13 findings with sections, repros and verified minimal fixes; negative results covering quiesce, API validation and leader transfer; and a report whose counts, evidence paths and fix snippets all reconcile. The audited implementation remains byte-identical to `../source`.
